In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of river‐basin nutrient models in stake‐holder dialogues.
the use of models in stakeholder panels and how the model output can be made useful for the stakeholders.
the use of river models to support local stakeholder dialogues in order to implement the WFD in a Swedish catchment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of models to stimulate stakeholder discussions can be a valuable tool to assist in WFD implementation, but that it will require further development and adaptation to local conditions.
the model‐stimulated discussions are valuable for the involved stakeholders, but that the model results need to be presented with caution and in a way that is understandable by the stakeholders.
the model‐based discussion material was perceived as valuable and useful by all the panellists, but that the model‐derived material should be complemented by other sources of information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of river‐basin models in stakeholder‐stimulated dialogues can provide a useful tool to facilitate local implementation.
a model approach to stakeholder dialogues has potential, although it requires further development.
a model‐based stakeholder dialogue can be used as an instrument to facilitate implementation of the WWD directive.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of river‐basin models in a stakeholder panel is a useful way to establish a common understanding among the participants of the existing status of the river basin and the pros and cons associated with the various remedial measures.
the stakeholders' perceptions of the model‐stimulated discussion material were not as important as the fact that the discussion was held.
the model‐based discussions can be useful to support the implementation of the WWD directive, if the models are developed in close collaboration with stakeholders.
